In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the single dilute nitric extraction (0.4 M) is a good extraction method for reactive elements in soil, although some elements are underestimated at low reactive element to reactive surface ratios.
the 0.43M nitric acid extraction is the most reliable extraction procedure to quantify the geochemical reactivity of elements in soils, but the method is still subject to further refinement.
0.43M HNO3 is the best option available at the moment for extraction of reactive element concentrations in soil.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

0.43M HNO3 is a good choice for extraction of geochemistry reactive elements from soil, except for Mo in which case 0.43 and 1 M HNO are equally suitable, and for Cu, Cr, and As in soils with high organic matter contents.

the dilute nitric extraction (0.4 M) is a suitable extraction to determine the geochemically reactive element concentrations in soil and soil-like materials, but that the model-predicted reactive element contents should be interpreted with caution for some elements.

the 0.43M HNO3 extraction is an appropriate method to estimate reactive element concentrations in soils, but that the method may underestimate the concentrations of elements that have a particularly high affinity to organic matter or oxids.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dilute nitric extraction is a suitable method for quantification of geochemically-reactive elements in soil, provided that the reactive concentration is high.
the 0.43M HNO3 extraction is a good choice to determine reactive elements in soil.
the 0.43M HNO3 extraction is a good alternative to the CaCl2 extraction, but that the latter should be preferred for the elements that were found to be over- or underestimated.
